stories.headline: Amazon Custom Chips Business Tops $20B Run Rate With Triple-Digit Growth as AWS Backlog Hits $364B

key_facts.fact: Amazon's custom chips business topped a $20 billion annual revenue run rate, growing at triple-digit rates year-over-year, encompassing Trainium and Graviton processors.
AWS revenue grew 28% YoY to $37.6 billion in Q1, its fastest growth in 15 quarters, while Amazon's overall Q1 revenue rose 17% to $181.5 billion.
AWS backlog reached $364 billion for the quarter, not including the recently announced Anthropic deal worth more than $100 billion.
OpenAI committed to consume about 2 GW of Trainium capacity through AWS beginning in 2027, while Anthropic secured up to 5 GW of current and future Trainium chips.
CEO Andy Jassy said memory and storage costs have 'skyrocketed,' with memory under the most pressure, reinforcing why hyperscalers are investing in custom silicon.

stories.headline: Anthropic Weighs $50B Round at $900B+ Valuation, Could Surpass OpenAI as Most Valuable AI Startup

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has received multiple preemptive offers to raise ~$50B at a valuation in the $850B–$900B range, according to half a dozen sources.
Anthropic's annual revenue run rate is now closer to $40B, up from roughly $9B at the end of 2025, driven largely by Claude Code and Cowork platforms.
Anthropic is expected to make a decision on the round at a board meeting in May; the round could be its final private fundraise before a potential IPO as early as October.
At $900B+, Anthropic would surpass OpenAI, which closed a $122B round at an $852B valuation in February. Anthropic shares on secondary markets are already trading at prices implying ~$1T valuation.
Anthropic raised its last round at a $380B valuation in February — making this a potential 2.4x jump in under three months.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches BioMysteryBench; Claude Mythos Solved ~30% of Questions That Stumped Human Experts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released BioMysteryBench, a bioinformatics benchmark using 99 real-world challenges with raw, messy datasets from actual research — designed to test creative problem-solving rather than textbook knowledge.
Claude Mythos solved approximately 30% of 23 questions that a panel of human bioinformatics experts could not answer, sometimes using strategies different from those attempted by humans.
Claude's scientific capabilities in biology are improving rapidly across model generations, with current models performing on par with human experts on the benchmark overall.
Unlike existing benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, LAB-Bench), BioMysteryBench focuses on open-ended research problems where there are many valid approaches, mirroring real scientific work.

stories.headline: Big Tech Q1 AI Capex Hits Record $130B; Microsoft AI Revenue at $37B Run Rate, Google Cloud Up 63%

key_facts.fact: Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon's combined Q1 capex hit a record $130B, with 2026 projected to reach $725B — up 77% from $410B in 2025.
Microsoft reported Q3 revenue of $82.9B (up 18% YoY) and said its AI business surpassed a $37B annual revenue run rate, up 123% YoY. Azure grew 40%.
Alphabet reported Q1 revenue of $109.9B (up 22% YoY), with Google Cloud hitting $20B (up 63%). It raised 2026 capex guidance to $180B–$190B, up from $175B–$185B.
Meta reported Q1 revenue of $56.31B (up 33% YoY) and raised 2026 capex guidance to $125B–$145B, up from $115B–$135B, driven by higher memory costs and AI compute demand.
AWS revenue rose 28% YoY to $37.6B, its fastest growth in 15 quarters. Amazon's chip business topped a $20B revenue run rate, growing triple digits YoY.
Google said paid subscriptions reached 350M in Q1, up 25M QoQ, while Gemini Enterprise paid MAUs grew 40% QoQ.

stories.headline: Big Tech Q1 Capex Hits Record $130B; Combined 2026 Spending Could Top $650B on AI Buildout

key_facts.fact: Meta raised its 2026 capex guidance to $125-145 billion (from $115-135B), citing higher memory prices and AI infrastructure expansion. Shares fell ~6% in after-hours.
Alphabet raised 2026 capex guidance to $180-190 billion (from $175-185B) and said 2027 capex would 'significantly increase.' Google Cloud revenue grew 63% YoY to $20B.
Amazon's Q1 capital spending was $43.2 billion, primarily tied to AWS and generative AI. Free cash flow collapsed 95% to $1.2 billion as operating cash flow was consumed by infrastructure investment.
Microsoft's AI business surpassed a $37 billion annual revenue run rate, up 123% YoY. Azure revenue grew 40% YoY. Microsoft 365 Copilot has 20M+ seats.
Industry analysis projects combined 2026 capex by Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft could exceed $650-725 billion, up 77% from ~$410 billion in 2025.

Meta's CFO said the company has 'continued to underestimate compute needs,' and Mark Zuckerberg said Meta is rolling out over 1 GW of custom AI silicon developed with Broadcom, plus adding significant AMD capacity alongside new Nvidia systems.

stories.headline: Fed Holds Rates in Most Divided Vote Since 1992 as Inflation Concerns Rise

key_facts.fact: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% in an 8-4 vote, the most divided decision since October 6, 1992.
Three policymakers (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) voted against including an easing bias in the statement; a fourth dissented in favor of a rate cut.
The Fed upgraded its inflation language from 'somewhat elevated' to 'elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices.'
This was Jerome Powell's last policy press conference as Fed chair; his term ends on May 15, with Kevin Warsh as his presumed successor.
Powell said the U.S. economy has been 'quite resilient' and is likely to keep growing above 2% this year due to solid consumer spending and data center investment.
Futures markets priced in little chance of a Fed rate cut by end of year; the March meeting minutes noted growing openness to a rate increase as the next move.

stories.headline: France Unveils Plan to Phase Out Coal by 2030, Oil by 2045, Gas by 2050

key_facts.fact: France announced a 'first of its kind' roadmap to phase out coal by 2030, oil by 2045, and gas for energy purposes by 2050, presented at the Santa Marta fossil fuel transition conference in Colombia.
The roadmap consolidates existing French climate targets under one umbrella; analysts said no other country had published such a clear and comprehensive fossil fuel exit plan.

Nearly 60 nations attended the Santa Marta conference, co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, including EU members, fossil fuel producers Canada and Norway, and developing oil giants Angola and Nigeria.
France generates only a fraction of its electricity from hydrocarbons thanks to nuclear power; the roadmap also commits to phasing out fossil fuel production and electrifying heating and transport.
The conference took place amid soaring fuel prices from the Iran war; France pushed ahead after a proposal for a global fossil fuel roadmap was blocked at the COP30 summit in November.

stories.headline: House Committees Probe Cursor Maker Anysphere and Airbnb Over Use of Chinese AI Models

key_facts.fact: House Homeland Security and China Select Committee chairs launched a joint investigation into national security risks of PRC-developed AI models from DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax.
Letters were sent to Anysphere (maker of Cursor) and Airbnb CEOs, requesting details about their use of Chinese-built AI and asking employees to participate in an in-person briefing.
Anysphere's Composer 2 model is built on Kimi, developed by Beijing-based Moonshot AI. Airbnb uses Alibaba's Qwen to power customer service tools.
Lawmakers cite concerns that Chinese companies use unauthorized model distillation to extract capabilities from American frontier AI systems, then repackage them without safeguards.
The White House OSTP has warned that foreign entities, primarily China-based, are conducting 'industrial-scale campaigns' to distill US frontier AI systems through proxy accounts.

stories.headline: Nvidia B300 Server Prices Nearly Double to ~$1M in China as Smuggling Crackdown Dries Up Supply

key_facts.fact: Nvidia B300 server prices in China have nearly doubled to about 7 million yuan (~$1 million) each, up from about 4 million yuan late last year, nearly double the ~$550,000 US price.
The scarcity followed U.S. authorities' March prosecution of Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw, a co-founder of Nvidia partner Supermicro, which disrupted the grey market supply channel.
Chinese tech companies avoid holding Nvidia hardware directly on their books for fear of U.S. sanctions exposure; some are exploring rentals at up to 190,000 yuan/month.
The B300 server houses eight B300 GPUs with 288 GB of HBM, delivering 14 petaFLOPS at FP4 precision. Nvidia began shipping it last September.
Nvidia still holds a 55% market share in China's AI chip market; Chinese AI models nearly tripled their share of global token usage to 32% in March 2026 from 5% a year earlier.
Uncertainty around H200 chip exports has fueled the B300 price surge; despite receiving approvals from both governments, the H200 has yet to be shipped to China.

stories.headline: Oil Surges to $126 Wartime High as Trump Lays Groundwork for Extended Iran Blockade

key_facts.fact: Brent crude briefly hit $126 per barrel on Thursday morning, a new wartime high, before falling back, as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed.
US gas prices jumped 7 cents to $4.30 per gallon, the highest since July 2022 and up 44% since the start of the Iran war.
Trump told top advisers he wants the naval blockade of Iranian ports to continue and his team has begun laying groundwork for a longer-term closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
The US has spent $25 billion on the Iran war so far, according to a senior Pentagon official who told lawmakers Wednesday.
Peace negotiations remain deadlocked; Pakistan could receive Iran's revised peace proposal by Friday, sources say.
Iran's oil minister urged the public to cut fuel consumption, calling conservation a 'religious duty,' as the country's Supreme Leader said foreign actors have no place in the Persian Gulf.

stories.headline: OpenAI Hits 10GW US Compute Capacity Goal Years Ahead of 2029 Target, Adding 3GW+ in 90 Days

key_facts.fact: OpenAI has signed contracts for 10 gigawatts of US AI computing capacity, a milestone it originally aimed to reach by 2029.
OpenAI added more than 3GW of committed compute capacity in the past 90 days alone.
A $16B Oracle data center in Michigan (for OpenAI) is under construction with Blackstone/PIMCO financing, targeting 1GW+ capacity by Q4 2027.

stories.headline: OpenAI Traces GPT-5.1's 'Goblin Problem' to RL Reward Leakage From Nerdy Personality Training

key_facts.fact: Starting with GPT-5.1, OpenAI's models increasingly used goblin and gremlin metaphors; 'goblin' usage rose 175% after GPT-5.1's launch, while 'gremlin' rose 52%.

The root cause was traced to the 'Nerdy' personality customization feature: its RL reward signal consistently scored outputs with creature words higher, even though Nerdy accounted for only 2.5% of responses but 66.7% of all goblin mentions.

The behavior spread via a feedback loop: the RL reward boosted creature-language under the Nerdy prompt, then the style transferred to non-Nerdy contexts through supervised fine-tuning on model-generated rollouts.
The Nerdy personality reward showed positive uplift for creature-word outputs in 76.2% of datasets audited, confirming systematic bias in the reward signal.
As goblin mentions increased under the Nerdy personality, they increased by nearly the same relative proportion in samples without it, demonstrating cross-context style transfer from RL training.

stories.headline: Qualcomm Enters Custom ASIC Market, Will Ship Data Center Chips to a Hyperscaler by Q4 2026

key_facts.fact: CEO Cristiano Amon confirmed Qualcomm is working on three types of data center chips: CPUs, inference accelerators, and custom ASICs, and will begin shipping to a large hyperscaler before year-end.
Qualcomm's custom ASIC engagement was enabled by its $2.4 billion acquisition of AlphaWave Semi last year, providing connectivity IP for data center designs.
Q2 FY2026 revenue came in at $10.6 billion (down 3% YoY), with adjusted EPS of $2.65 beating the $2.56 consensus estimate. Shares surged ~15% in after-hours trading.
The data center push enters a market dominated by Broadcom (projected ~60% market share in custom ASICs) and Marvell. Qualcomm anticipates data center revenue beginning in fiscal 2028.
Amon said Q3 would mark the bottom for Chinese handset revenue and that the smartphone market will rebound: 'We can now call the bottom.'

stories.headline: Samsung Q1 Operating Profit Jumps 8x to Record $40B on AI Memory Demand; Warns 2027 Shortage Deepens

key_facts.fact: Samsung Q1 operating profit surged more than eightfold to ₩57.23 trillion (~$40.1B) from ₩6.68 trillion a year earlier; revenue climbed 69% to ₩133.87 trillion (~$93.7B) — both all-time records.
The Device Solutions (semiconductor) division posted ₩53.7 trillion in operating profit — a 48.8x increase from ₩1.1 trillion a year ago — driven by AI chip demand and rising memory prices.
Samsung mass-produced HBM4 as an industry first and will ship next-generation HBM4E customer samples in Q2, ahead of competitors.
Samsung warned the memory shortage will worsen in 2027 as customers are already placing orders for that year, creating a projected supply gap larger than 2026.
In the second half of 2026, Samsung will mass-produce a new 4nm language processing unit (LPU) for AI and HPC customers through its foundry business.

stories.headline: Samsung Q1 Chip Profit Jumps 49x to Record $36B as Memory Shortage Set to Worsen in 2027

key_facts.fact: Samsung Q1 operating profit reached a record ₩57.2 trillion ($40.1B), with the chip division accounting for ₩53.7 trillion ($36.15B) — a 49-fold year-over-year increase from ₩1.1 trillion.
Revenue rose 69% YoY to ₩133.9 trillion ($93.7B), an all-time quarterly high, beating the analyst estimate of ~₩130 trillion.

Samsung warned the memory supply-demand gap will widen further in 2027: 'Based solely on the demand currently received for 2027, the supply-to-demand gap for 2027 is set to widen even further than in 2026.'
Samsung started the industry's first mass-production sales of HBM4 chips and SOCAMM2 modules for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, and will deliver HBM4E samples in Q2 2026.
HBM revenue is forecast to more than triple this year versus last year, with HBM4's share of total HBM revenue expected to exceed 50% starting in Q3 2026.
Samsung has signed multi-year binding contracts with customers hoping to lock in supplies, and said it expects to increase capital expenditure sharply this year to meet AI demand.
DRAM ASPs rose roughly 90-95% sequentially from Q4 to Q1, signaling sharp tightening in memory markets tied to AI-driven demand.

stories.headline: SoftBank Plans Roze AI Robotics and Data Center Company, Eyes $100B U.S. IPO as Early as 2026

key_facts.fact: SoftBank is creating a new company called Roze AI that will focus on building data centers in the U.S. and using autonomous robots to improve construction efficiency.
SoftBank is targeting a valuation of about $100 billion and aiming to list Roze as early as the second half of 2026, driven by founder Masayoshi Son.
Roze could bundle existing SoftBank portfolio assets including energy, land, infrastructure, and ABB Robotics, which SoftBank agreed to buy last year.
The IPO would help offset SoftBank's massive AI commitments, including more than $30 billion pledged to OpenAI and its role in the $500 billion Stargate project.
Some SoftBank executives have expressed skepticism about the valuation target and proposed IPO timeline, partly due to uncertainties from the Middle East conflict.

stories.headline: SpaceX Falcon Heavy Returns After 18-Month Gap, Launches ViaSat-3 F3 Satellite

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy lifted off at 10:13 a.m. EDT on April 29 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A, its first flight since October 2024's Europa Clipper mission.
The mission carried ViaSat-3 F3, a 6.6-ton broadband satellite designed to deliver over 1 Tbps of throughput to the Asia-Pacific region, completing Viasat's three-satellite constellation.
Both side boosters successfully landed at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, while the center core was expended.
Viasat confirmed initial signal acquisition minutes after satellite separation, confirming the spacecraft is healthy in orbit; service entry is expected by late summer 2026.
Several additional Falcon Heavy missions are planned for 2026, including the Griffin lunar lander for Artemis and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

stories.headline: US and 5 Latin American Nations Condemn China's Retaliation Over Panama Canal Ports

key_facts.fact: Bolivia, Costa Rica, Guyana, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, and the US released a joint statement criticizing China's 'targeted economic pressure' on Panamanian-flagged ships.
China detained nearly 70 Panamanian-flagged ships in March, far exceeding historical norms, according to the US Federal Maritime Commission.
The retaliation followed Panama's Supreme Court annulling contracts that allowed CK Hutchison's subsidiary to administer the Balboa and Cristobal port terminals.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was 'deeply concerned' by China's economic pressure, calling it a threat to sovereignty.
China also retaliated against Maersk and MSC, whose subsidiaries were granted contracts to replace CK Hutchison; COSCO suspended operations at the Balboa terminal.

stories.headline: US Sanctions 35 Iran-Linked Entities, Warns Chinese Refiners Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit

key_facts.fact: The US Treasury sanctioned 35 entities and individuals for their roles in Iran's shadow banking sector, which facilitated tens of billions of dollars in sanctions evasion.
Treasury warned financial institutions they face sanctions risk over dealings with Chinese teapot refineries in Shandong province that process Iranian oil.
China purchases approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports, with teapot refineries accounting for the majority of these imports.
Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iran's Kharg Island export terminal is 'soon nearing storage capacity,' which could force Tehran to cut production and lose $170 million in daily revenue.
The moves come less than a month before Trump's planned visit to Beijing, adding another irritant to US-China relations.
